q: The lowest normal systolic BP for an 8-year-old is about:
By IMCI, fast breathing in a 3-year-old is a rate of:
e: IMCI: ≥ 60 under 2 months, ≥ 50 at 2–12 months, ≥ 40 at 1–5 years.

o: With a tape along the back
e: Under 2 years the length is measured lying down on a length board.

q: A boy's height has crossed centiles downwards while his weight is preserved. The most likely cause is:
e: Height falling first with weight kept or high suggests an endocrine cause.

q: A short boy has normal growth velocity, delayed bone age and a father who had late puberty. The diagnosis is:
e: Constitutional delay: normal velocity, delayed bone age, late puberty in a parent.

q: Which test is done in every girl with unexplained short stature?
e: Turner syndrome may have few features; a karyotype excludes it.

q: A child crawls, pulls to stand, has an immature pincer grasp and stranger anxiety. The developmental age is:
A 2-year-old has normal motor and social skills but says only one word. The first investigation is:
e: Isolated speech delay needs a hearing test first.
